report_name: Ransomware Landscape Fragments as 61 New Groups Emerge in H1 2026

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: The most prolific ransomware group between March 2025 and March 2026, claiming 1,358 victims. Leads the top five most active groups in a fragmented ransomware ecosystem.

threat_actors.name: Akira
threat_actors.description: The second most active ransomware group between March 2025 and March 2026, with 749 publicly claimed victims.

threat_actors.name: INC Ransom
threat_actors.description: The third most active ransomware group between March 2025 and March 2026, responsible for 436 victims.

threat_actors.name: Play
threat_actors.description: One of the top five most active ransomware groups between March 2025 and March 2026.

threat_actors.name: LockBit
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that remains in the top five most active groups despite law enforcement disruptions.

threat_actors.name: The Gentlemen
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group mentioned as battling for dominance in the current threat landscape.

threat_actors.name: Conti
threat_actors.description: A formerly dominant ransomware group, mentioned as an example of a single player that once defined the market before its fragmentation.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups for initial access by exploiting vulnerabilities in VPNs and other edge devices.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups for initial access, likely through spearphishing campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups for initial access via stolen credentials purchased from initial access brokers.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups for defense evasion by disabling security products.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: A standard practice for ransomware groups as part of double extortion tactics.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Used by ransomware groups to exfiltrate data as part of double extortion tactics.

attack_patterns.name: Network Denial of Service
attack_patterns.description: Used by some ransomware groups as part of triple extortion tactics, in addition to data exfiltration and encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware groups inhibit system recovery by deleting volume shadow copies using tools like wmic.exe.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-hop Proxy
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operations may use anonymization networks like Tor for command and control or data exfiltration.

indicators.name: WMIC Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: WMIC Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8c1f9a-3e4d-4b1a-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of wmic.exe to delete shadow copies, a common ransomware TTP to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/new-ransomware-weekly/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-21
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'shadowcopy'
      - 'delete'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a common ransomware technique to prevent system recovery by deleting volume shadow copies using the Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line (WMIC) utility.

indicators.name: Generic Ransom Note Creation (README.txt)
indicators.pattern:
title: Generic Ransom Note Creation (README.txt)
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a file named README.txt, which is a common name for ransomware notes. This rule may be noisy and should be correlated with other indicators.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/new-ransomware-weekly/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-21
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software that creates README.txt files.
level: low
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\README.txt'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a file named 'README.txt', a common filename for ransom notes left by ransomware.

indicators.name: Potential Tor Network Connection
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Tor Network Connection
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-4a1b-8c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network connections on common Tor ports (9001, 9050, 9051). This may indicate the use of Tor for C2 or other anonymized activity.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/new-ransomware-weekly/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-21
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate applications using these ports for other purposes.
level: low
tags:
  - attack.t1090.003
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort:
      - 9001
      - 9050
      - 9051
    Initiated: true
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network traffic patterns indicative of connections to the Tor network, which can be used by threat actors for anonymized command and control.
